- **Health**: a11y_violations

## Interaction Behavior

RadioField is a Field.Root wrapper, not a control: hover, press, tap-scale, and the informative-blue focus halo all belong to the inner Radio. Two things the wrapper uniquely owns. First, INTEGRATED SINGLE (no Radio children) can toggle OFF — re-clicking the selected circle clears the value to `''` via a click-capture handler, which a normal radio cannot do. Second, that circle uses `labelWrapper="div"`, so the field `Field.Label` is a real `<label>` associated through Base UI `htmlFor`; the field description is `aria-describedby` only and is not inside that label. Multi-option mode is a fieldset+legend above a normal RadioGroup that still arrows-to-select.

**Hover**
- RadioField.module.css has no `:hover` rule. Hover chrome is the inner Radio's: the 16–24px circle tints, wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`.
- Unchecked hover fills the circle with the parent-surface role's `--{Role}-Hover` (Neutral on a bare page), not the field's `appearance`. Checked hover steps fill and border to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover`.
- There is no hover styling on the field label or description.

**Press**
- The inner Radio circle scales UP on press (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up`, 7%) and tints to `--{Role}-Pressed` (unchecked) or `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` (checked).
- Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded.
- In integrated single, a press on an ALREADY-SELECTED circle is intercepted in capture and clears the value instead of being a no-op — that is the whole point of the wrapper's `onClickCapture`.

**Focus**
- Focus lands on the inner `role="radio"` span, never on the Field.Label. The halo is Radio's two-layer ring whose OUTER colour is `--Informative-Bold`, not `--Focus-Outline` — a `positive` or `negative` option still focuses informative-blue.
- `:focus-visible` only on the circle; clicking the field label activates the control but does not paint the ring (mouse click).
- `readOnly` radios stay focusable (Base UI `readOnly`, not `disabled`). RadioField then strips `aria-readonly` from `[role="radio"]` because that attribute is invalid there; `data-readonly` styling remains.

**Keyboard**
- RadioField adds no key handlers. Keyboard is the inner RadioGroup: `Space` selects, `Enter` is deliberately swallowed, arrow keys move AND select, `Home` / `End` do nothing (`enableHomeAndEndKeys: false` on RadioGroup).
- In multi-option mode the field `Field.Label` lives in a `<legend>` and does not itself select an option; each child Radio uses the default native `<label>` wrapper, so that option's own label/description text is the hit target.
- In integrated single the Radio is `labelWrapper="div"` with `children={null}`. The visible name is `aria-labelledby` pointing at a span inside `Field.Label`, and Base UI's `htmlFor` also associates that `<label>` with the radio's hidden input, so clicking the field label text activates the control.
- The field description is a `Field.Description` sibling (`aria-describedby` on the group) — it is not a `<label>` and is not a toggle hit target.
- The capture-to-clear path is a mouse `onClickCapture` on the radio wrapper. Whether a keyboard Space on an already-selected integrated radio also clears is not covered by tests.

**Selected / checked**
- Multi-option selection is owned by the inner RadioGroup via `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`. Selecting one option deselects the others; you cannot empty the group by re-clicking the selected option.
- Integrated single (no children) is the exception: re-clicking the selected circle fires `onValueChange('')` and `onCheckedChange(false)` and sets `aria-checked="false"` — covered by a unit test. A second click selects again (`singleOptionValue`, default `'on'`).
- Integrated single can be driven as a boolean (`checked` / `defaultChecked` / `onCheckedChange`) or as a string (`value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`); when neither is controlled, the wrapper holds internal state so the clear-to-empty path can actually stick (Base UI will not fire change on re-clicking a selected radio by itself).
- Checked fill/dot colours are Radio's: `--{Role}-Bold` circle, `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y` dot. `appearance` on the field is forwarded onto every option.

**Disabled**
- `disabled` is passed to `Field.Root`, the RadioGroup, and every enhanced child Radio, and `data-disabled` is set on the label stack so the label/description drop to `--Text-Low`.
- The inner Radio's `not-allowed` cursor IS observable: the circle is `pointer-events: none`, so the pointer falls through to Radio's `<label>`/`<div>` wrapper, which also declares `not-allowed` (see the Radio docs). In integrated single that wrapper is a `<div>`, but it still carries the cursor.
- `readOnly` forwards to each Radio for interaction lock and `data-readonly` ink, and RadioField strips the invalid `aria-readonly` from the `role="radio"` node. The capture-to-clear handler also no-ops when `disabled` or `readOnly`.

**Touch**
- Hover tints never apply on touch-only devices; the inner Radio's +7% press scale plus the pressed tint are the response to a tap on the circle.
- In integrated single the field `Field.Label` extends the hit target across the label text, but the description row is not part of that label. In multi-option mode each option's own Radio `<label>` (label + that option's description) is the hit target — the fieldset legend is not.
- Nothing pads the row to 44px; the circle itself is 16/20/24px at S/M/L.

## Intent and Purpose

- **Intent**: Mutually exclusive segmented control for switching between related views or filters. Wraps Base UI ToggleGroup. Supports track emphasis, attention-driven selected states, equal-width layout, text and icon-only segments, and start (icon) / end (CounterBadge) slots.
- **Task contexts**: navigation, filter, toggle, selection, segmented
- **Sentiments**: neutral

## Composition Rules

- **Requires**: -
- **Allows**: children
- **Forbids**: -

## Variant Logic

- **high**: use when High
- **medium**: use when Medium
- **low**: use when Low

## Relationships and Dependencies

- **Related**: -
- **Escalates to**: -
- **Degrades to**: -
- **Groups with**: -

## Context Signals

- **Density**: compact, default, open
- **Modality**: desktop, mobile
- **Brand**: theme-scope aware, recipe-driven
- **Mode**: light, dark, surface-context

## Observability Hooks

- **Track**: -
- **Health**: a11y_violations

## Interaction Behavior

SegmentedControl is a required single-select ToggleGroup whose selected fill is a sliding pill behind the segments, not a background on the item. Unselected hover is a second pill that follows the cursor in JS; selected hover/press tint that same active pill via `:has()`, so there is never a second fill racing the glide. Arrow keys move focus only — `Enter` / `Space` / click commit — and the currently selected segment cannot be turned off.

**Hover**
- Unselected hover does not paint the item: a `.hoverIndicator` pill glides to the hovered segment in `--{TrackRole}-Subtle` at `trackEmphasis="high"`, or `--{TrackRole}-Minimal` at medium/low. The item only keeps `--{TrackRole}-High` text.
- The pill is driven by `pointermove` on the group. `pointerType === "touch"` is ignored, and the pill hides when the pointer is over a disabled or already-selected (`[data-pressed]`) segment.
- Selected hover tints the `.activeIndicator` itself via `:has(.item[data-pressed]:hover)`: `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` at `attention="high"`, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` at medium, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` of the track role at low.
- Both hover fills are wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck hover pill.

**Press**
- An unselected press fills the item's state-layer with the track pressed token (`--{TrackRole}-Subtle-Pressed` at high track emphasis, `--{TrackRole}-Pressed` at medium/low) — this is fill-on-the-item, not the hover pill, and is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded.
- A selected press tints the active pill via `:has(.item[data-pressed]:active)` to `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` / `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` / track `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` by attention.
- There is no tap-scale on the segment. Feedback is pill + text colour only.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo on the inner state-layer: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring.
- A high-attention selected segment prepends `--Elevation-1` to that same `box-shadow` so the raised pill and the halo coexist.
- `:focus` only clears the native outline; the ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click does not paint it.

**Keyboard**
- Each segment is a native `<button aria-pressed>`. `Enter` / `Space` select it; they do not live in OneUI code — Base UI Toggle + `useButton` handle them.
- `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move focus only. They do not change the selected segment. `Home` / `End` jump focus to the first / last enabled segment. `loopFocus` is always on.
- Disabled segments are natively `disabled`, so arrows skip them.
- Clicking or key-activating the already-selected segment would toggle it off in Base UI, but the group's `onValueChange` ignores an empty array, so selection is required — the pill never disappears.

**Selected / checked**
- Selected is Base UI Toggle `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and `[data-pressed]`. The fill lives on `.activeIndicator`, not on the item — the item's state-layer only changes text colour.
- `attention="high"`: pill is `--{Role}-Bold` (or `--{Role}-Material-Fill` when the role has a material) plus `--Elevation-1`, text `--{Role}-Bold-High`. Medium: `--{Role}-Subtle` fill, `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text. Low: track-role `--{Role}-Subtle` fill, track `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text.
- On a selection change `.activeIndicator` glides to the new segment: `transform: translateX(...)` plus a `width` transition over `--Motion-Duration-L` / `--Motion-Easing-Transition-Moderate`. It only eases while continuously visible; a pill appearing fresh (through `display` + `allow-discrete`) fades in at the target spot instead of sliding from a stale position.
- The one place motion is intentionally killed is resize — the pill is repositioned with `transition: none` for a single frame so a window resize never replays the tap-to-select glide.

**Disabled**
- A disabled group sets `[data-disabled]` and dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` with `cursor: not-allowed`. A per-item `disabled` is a native `disabled` attribute plus `pointer-events: none`.
- Because the item is natively disabled with `pointer-events: none`, `cursor: not-allowed` on the item is not observable — the pointer shows the group's cursor. This is the known system-wide gap (docs/design/disabled-states.md).
- Hover pill tracking skips `[data-disabled]` items, and every hover/press selector excludes them.

**Touch**
- Touch pointers never drive the hover pill (`pointerType === "touch"` returns before measuring), so a tap does not leave a hover fill on the next segment.
- The pressed fill on an unselected segment, then the active pill glide, are the entire tap response.

# SelectableButton Machine-Readable Documentation

_Generated from source metadata. Do not edit manually._

## Intent and Purpose

- **Intent**: Toggle button with text label and optional start/end slots for binary selection within groups.
- **Task contexts**: filter-toggle, option-selection, segmented-control, toolbar-toggle
- **Sentiments**: neutral, positive

## Composition Rules

- **Requires**: children (text label) or aria-label
- **Allows**: start/end slots (icon, badge), contained/uncontained mode, condensed mode, fullWidth
- **Forbids**: use for navigation (use Button instead), nested interactive elements

## Variant Logic

- **high attention**: use when selected state needs bold fill emphasis
- **medium attention**: use when selected state with subtle tinted fill
- **low attention**: use when selected state with ghost appearance and accent border

## Relationships and Dependencies

- **Related**: SelectableIconButton, SelectableSingleTextButton, Button, Toggle, ToggleGroup
- **Escalates to**: -
- **Degrades to**: -
- **Groups with**: ToggleGroup

## Context Signals

- **Density**: compact, default, open
- **Modality**: desktop, mobile
- **Brand**: theme-scope aware, recipe-driven
- **Mode**: light, dark, surface-context

## Observability Hooks

- **Track**: select, deselect
- **Health**: a11y_violations, adoption_rate

## Interaction Behavior

SelectableButton is a Base UI Toggle, so every click flips `aria-pressed` — and unlike Chip, it starts UNSELECTED (`defaultSelected` defaults to `false`). Attention colours the SELECTED look only; unselected is always a muted ghost regardless of attention. Press feedback is a scale DOWN (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`, 3%; 1% when `fullWidth`) with NO pressed fill token at all. `contained={false}` strips the pill so hover fills never apply and selection is colour-only. `loading` implies disabled: the start/label/end slots go to `opacity: 0` and a centred spinner takes over without the button changing size.

**Hover**
- Every hover rule is wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)` and excluded for `[data-contained="false"]` and `[data-disabled]`.
- UNSELECTED (contained) tints the transparent rest fill to `--{Role}-Hover`.
- SELECTED at `attention="high"` steps the fill to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` (or keeps `--{Role}-Material-Fill` when a metallic gradient is assigned); at `medium` it steps to `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`; at `low` it ADDS a `--{Role}-Hover` fill over the rest transparent-plus-accent-hairline.
- Label and icon colours never change on hover — only the background.
- `contained={false}` has no hover fill and no hover colour shift, so an inline selectable is visually inert on hover.

**Press**
- The entire button scales DOWN: `scale(1 - tapScale/100)` with `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default` at 3%, dropping to `--Motion-Tap-Scale-FullWidth` (1%) when `fullWidth`. This is the same direction as Button, opposite to SelectableIconButton / SelectableSingleTextButton which grow.
- There is no `:active` fill, border, or text-colour rule — press colour feedback does not exist. The squash is the entire pressed look.
- The scale rule is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded and is NOT excluded for `contained={false}`, so an uncontained selectable still squashes on tap even though its colours do not change.
- Qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring.
- `:focus` alone only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click selects without painting a halo.
- With `contained={false}` the button sets `border-radius: 0` and has no padding, so the halo is a tight square around the text rather than a pill ring.

**Keyboard**
- Base UI Toggle renders a native `<button aria-pressed>`, so `Enter` and `Space` both toggle — both paths are covered by tests.
- Controlled via `selected` / `onSelectedChange`; uncontrolled via `defaultSelected` (default `false`). Pass `value` when nesting inside a ToggleGroup.
- Disabled and loading are natively `disabled`, so they are out of the tab order and cannot toggle.

**Selected / checked**
- Selected maps to Base UI Toggle's `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and matched in CSS with `[data-pressed]`.
- It defaults to FALSE in uncontrolled mode — a bare `<SelectableButton>Like</SelectableButton>` renders unselected. This is the opposite of Chip, which defaults to selected.
- `attention` colours the SELECTED contained look only: high → `--{Role}-Bold` fill with `--{Role}-Bold-High` text and a transparent border; medium → `--{Role}-Subtle` fill with `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text; low → transparent fill with a `--{Role}-Bold` hairline and accent text. Unselected is always transparent + `--{Role}-Medium-Text` + `--{Role}-Stroke-Low` hairline, ignoring attention.
- `contained={false}` never paints a pill: unselected high uses `--{Role}-High` text, unselected medium/low use `--{Role}-Medium-Text`; selected high uses `--{Role}-TintedA11y`, selected medium/low use `--{Role}-High`.
- Start/end slot icons inherit `currentColor` and, when selected contained high, are remapped onto `--{Role}-Bold-High` so they stay readable on the bold fill.

**Loading**
- `loading` implies disabled — `isDisabled = disabled || loading` — so the native `disabled` attribute is set and `onSelectedChange` stops firing.
- `aria-busy="true"` and `data-loading` are set; the `.loading` class is applied.
- The start slot, label, and end slot go to `opacity: 0` rather than `display: none`, which keeps their boxes in layout — the button does not resize — and keeps the label in the accessibility tree.
- The spinner is absolutely positioned across the button's box, so it lands centred over the hidden content.

**Disabled**
- `disabled` (and loading) emit Base UI's `data-disabled`, which dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed` plus `pointer-events: none`.
- Because the underlying button is natively `disabled` AND has `pointer-events: none`, the `not-allowed` cursor is not observable — the pointer shows the parent's cursor. Known, accepted system-wide gap (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
- Every hover fill and the tap-scale are qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`. Disabling does not clear the selected styling — it only dims whatever selected/unselected look was showing.

**Touch**
- Hover fills never apply on touch-only devices; the 3% (or 1% full-width) squash is the entire visual response to a tap, because there is no pressed fill.
- The whole pill is the hit target — start, label, and end sit inside the toggle button.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appearance` | `SelectableButtonAppearance` | No | - | Multi-accent appearance role. 'auto' resolves to 'primary'. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| `attention` | `SelectableButtonAttention` | No | - | Attention level — determines the visual prominence of the SELECTED state. high → bold fill; medium → subtle fill; low → ghost with accent border. The UNSELECTED state is always muted ghost regardless of attention. Default: 'high'. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | No | - | Text label content |
| `className` | `string` | No | - | Additional class name |
| `condensed` | `boolean` | No | - | Condensed mode: reduces height and horizontal padding while keeping the same typography. Only applies when contained=true. |
| `contained` | `boolean` | No | - | When true (default), renders a pill container with background, border, and padding. When false, renders inline text/icon only — no background, border, or padding. condensed and fullWidth do not apply when contained=false. |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean` | No | - | Default selected state (uncontrolled). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | No | - | Whether the button is disabled. |
| `end` | `ReactNode` | No | - | Content to render after the label (icon, etc.) |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | No | - | Stretch to fill container width. Only applies when contained=true. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | No | - | Loading state — disables interaction and shows reduced opacity. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(selected: boolean) => void` | No | - | Called when selected state changes. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | No | - | Selected state (controlled). Maps to Toggle pressed. |
| `size` | `SelectableButtonSize` | No | - | Button size. Default: 'm'. |
| `start` | `ReactNode` | No | - | Content to render before the label (icon, etc.) |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | No | - | Inline styles |
| `value` | `string` | No | - | Value for use within ToggleGroup. |

| `start` | Icon | `iconSize`, `gap` |

<SelectableButton>Option A</SelectableButton>

- **Track**: select, deselect
- **Health**: a11y_violations, adoption_rate

## Interaction Behavior

SelectableSingleTextButton is a Base UI Toggle for a 1–2 character circular label, so every click flips `aria-pressed` and it starts UNSELECTED. Attention colours the SELECTED look only; unselected is always a muted ghost with a `--{Role}-Stroke-Low` hairline. It scales UP on press (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up`, 7%) with NO pressed fill token — the same grow-not-squash direction as SelectableIconButton, opposite SelectableButton. There is no `contained={false}`. `loading` implies disabled and injects a spinner, but the CSS that would hide the letters is keyed off a `.loading` class the component never applies, so the characters stay visible beside the spinner.

**Hover**
- Every hover rule is wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)` and excluded for `[data-disabled]`.
- UNSELECTED tints the transparent rest fill to `--{Role}-Hover`.
- SELECTED at `attention="high"` steps the fill to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` (or keeps `--{Role}-Material-Fill`); at `medium` it steps to `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`; at `low` it ADDS a `--{Role}-Hover` fill over the rest transparent-plus-accent-hairline.
- Label colour never changes on hover — only the background.

**Press**
- The whole circle scales UP: `scale(calc(1 + var(--_tap-direction) * var(--_tap-scale) / 100))` with `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` at 7%. SelectableButton scales DOWN; this matches IconButton and SelectableIconButton.
- There is no `:active` fill, border, or text-colour rule — the scale-up is the entire pressed look.
- Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a finger tap gets the same grow a mouse press does.
- Qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring.
- `:focus` alone only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`.
- The halo follows `--SelectableSingleTextButton-borderRadius` (default `--Shape-Pill`).

**Keyboard**
- Base UI Toggle renders a native `<button aria-pressed>`, so `Enter` and `Space` both toggle.
- Controlled via `selected` / `onSelectedChange`; uncontrolled via `defaultSelected` (unset → unselected). Pass `value` when nesting inside a ToggleGroup.
- Disabled and loading are natively `disabled`, so they are out of the tab order and cannot toggle — covered by a unit test.

**Selected / checked**
- Selected maps to Base UI Toggle's `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and matched in CSS with `[data-pressed]`.
- It defaults to unselected in uncontrolled mode.
- `attention` colours the SELECTED look only: high → `--{Role}-Bold` fill with `--{Role}-Bold-High` text and a transparent border; medium → `--{Role}-Subtle` fill with `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text; low → transparent fill with a `--{Role}-Bold` hairline and accent text.
- Unselected is always transparent + `--{Role}-Medium-Text` + `--{Role}-Stroke-Low` hairline, ignoring attention — there is no uncontained variant to change that.

**Loading**
- `loading` implies disabled — `isDisabled = disabled || loading` — so the native `disabled` attribute is set, `aria-busy` / `data-loading` are set, and `onSelectedChange` stops firing.
- A spinner is injected as a sibling of the still-rendered label. The CSS that would hide that label (`.loading .label { opacity: 0 }`) and absolutely centre the spinner is keyed off a `.loading` class that SelectableSingleTextButton never applies, so the letters stay visible beside the spinner and the circle can grow.
- Tests only assert that a spinner SVG is present and that the toggle is blocked — they do not assert the label is hidden.

**Disabled**
- `data-disabled` dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed` plus `pointer-events: none`.
- Because the element is natively `disabled` AND has `pointer-events: none`, the `not-allowed` cursor is not observable — the pointer shows the parent's cursor. Known, accepted system-wide gap (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
- Hover fills and the tap-scale are qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`. Disabling does not clear the selected styling — it only dims it.

**Touch**
- Hover fills never apply on touch-only devices; the 7% scale-up is the entire visual response to a tap, because there is no pressed fill.
- Growing on press is the right direction for a control this small — the circle expands out from under the fingertip that is covering the letters.

**Press**

- The whole button scales UP: `scale(calc(1 + var(--_tap-direction) * var(--_tap-scale) / 100))` with `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` at 7% and `--_tap-direction: 1`. Button scales DOWN; this matches IconButton instead.

## Observability Hooks

## Interaction Behavior

Slider is a Base UI slider whose thumb grows to an explicit active diameter on hover, drag, and keyboard focus — not a `scale()` squash, because Figma's +2/+4/+4 growth is not a constant ratio. A click on the track jumps the nearest thumb to that point and captures the pointer; a click on the thumb itself waits for movement. Keyboard arrows accelerate like a macOS slider, while `Home` / `End` still jump to the bounds through Base UI.

**Hover**
- Hover grows the knob dot from its idle diameter to the per-size active diameter (`--_knob-dot-active-size`), interpolating `width` / `height` rather than using `transform: scale()`.
- Wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck grown knob.
- In `showTooltip="auto"` (the default) the value bubble also appears above the knob (or to the right when vertical) on that same hover.
- The rail and fill colours do not change on hover — only the knob diameter, plus the tooltip.

**Press**
- Pointer-down on the THUMB does not jump the value; it marks `[data-knob-active]` / `[data-dragging]`, switches the cursor to `grabbing`, and grows the dot to the same active diameter as hover.
- Pointer-down on the TRACK (the Control, including empty rail) immediately sets the nearest enabled thumb to that point (`trackPress`) and then captures the pointer for the drag. Range sliders pick the closest thumb by midpoint distance.
- The Control calls `setPointerCapture` on the pointer id, so the drag keeps updating if the finger leaves the track.
- `snapToSteps` (default `true`) uses `step` as the drag increment. `snapToSteps={false}` uses `min(step, (max-min)/1000)` so dragging is nearly continuous; keyboard still uses the real `step`.
- In `showTooltip="auto"` the value bubble is also shown throughout the drag, not only on hover/focus: `[data-dragging]` on the thumb is one of its visibility triggers (alongside `[data-open]`, `:has(:focus-visible)`, and forced states), so the current value stays readable while the finger or cursor moves.
- `onValueCommitted` fires on pointer-up / pointer-cancel, which also clears `activeKnobIndex` so the knob shrinks back and the drag-driven bubble hides.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus grows the knob to the active diameter and draws the two-layer halo on the DOT: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer ring in `--Informative-Bold` (always Informative, not the slider's appearance role).
- The halo is `:has(:focus-visible)` on the thumb, so a mouse click that focuses the hidden range input does not paint it.
- In `showTooltip="auto"` the bubble also appears for `:focus-visible`. `showTooltip="always"` pins it open via `[data-open]`; `false` omits the bubble entirely.

**Keyboard**
- A capture-phase handler on the thumb input intercepts `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (horizontal) or `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (vertical), `PageUp` / `PageDown`, and `Shift+Arrow`. It `preventDefault`s and `stopPropagation`s so ancestors never see those keys.
- First presses move by `step`. Held repeats accelerate: ×2 after 4 repeats, ×5 after 12, then `largeStep` (default 10) after 24. `Shift` and `PageUp` / `PageDown` always use `largeStep`.
- `Home` / `End` are NOT intercepted — Base UI jumps to `min` / `max`, or to the neighbouring thumb minus `minStepsBetweenValues` in range mode.
- On a horizontal slider, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` fall through the acceleration hook (it returns without preventing) and Base UI steps them by Root's `step` prop — that is `dragStep`, so with `snapToSteps={false}` those keys use the fine increment, not the public `step`. The same applies to `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` on a vertical slider.
- `readOnly` keeps the thumb focusable and sets `aria-readonly`, but cancels Base UI's change (`eventDetails.cancel()`) and does not attach the accelerator. `disabled` does not attach it either.

**Disabled**
- `disabled` dims the root to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed`. The Control and the hidden range input get `pointer-events: none`.
- The not-allowed cursor is declared on the root, which is not the natively disabled input, so it is observable — this is not the Button-style cursor gap.
- `readOnly` is a separate axis: it does not dim, does not set `pointer-events: none`, and stays in the tab order; it only rejects value changes.

**Touch**
- The thumb hit target is `--Spacing-12` (48px) regardless of knob size, so the visual dot can be 2px while the finger still has a 48×48 target.
- The root and Control set `touch-action: none` so a drag does not scroll the page.
- Hover growth is `(hover: hover)`-guarded; a touch drag still grows the knob via `[data-knob-active]` / `[data-dragging]`, which are not hover-gated.

## Interaction Behavior

Stepper is a Base UI NumberField whose visible value is an odometer, not the native input: each place's digit strip translateY-rolls on a CSS `transform` transition (`--Motion-Duration-L` / `--Motion-Easing-Transition-Moderate`) so a held auto-repeat retargets instead of restarting. When the digit count changes the pill width animates too — each `.place` transitions `width`, a new place entering from `@starting-style { width: 0 }` and a removed one collapsing to `0` on `[data-exiting]`, so 9→10 eases the capsule wider and 10→9 shrinks it. The affected leading digit is a `.riser` that translateY-rolls in from below (or sinks out) in sync, its entrance staggered by `--Stepper-leadDelay` (`--Motion-Offset-L`); `prefers-reduced-motion` and `data-subtle-motion` set `transition: none` on all of it. The +/− controls are IconButtons. A comment on `.button` zeros `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`, but those 1:1 buttons actually scale UP via `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up`; `overflow: clip` on the pill is what keeps the overlay inside. Direct typing reveals the real input; a +/− press that focuses the input on purpose does not.

**Hover**
- Hover lives on the inner IconButtons, not the pill. Stepper remaps their ghost hover slots onto its attention tokens: `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` at `attention="high"`, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` at medium, `--Neutral-Hover` (auto) at low and for every `type="input"` attention.
- Those IconButton hover fills are `(hover: hover)`-guarded in IconButton's own CSS, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck overlay.
- The pill background itself does not change on hover.

**Press**
- Press fill on +/− follows the same remapped slots: `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` / `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` / `--Neutral-Pressed` by attention.
- `.button` sets `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default: 0` with a comment claiming this zeros IconButton squash. Current 1:1 IconButtons (Stepper uses sizes 4 / 6 / 8 / 10) actually scale UP via `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` (default 7%) — they do not read `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`. The pill's `overflow: clip` is what contains that grow so the overlay never paints outside the capsule.
- Holding +/− uses Base UI `usePressAndHold`: the first tick steps, then auto-repeat continues to fire `incrementValue`. Releasing commits via `onValueCommitted`. The odometer transition retargets, so a hold scrolls continuously instead of restarting each tick.
- At `min` / `max` that button is natively disabled by Base UI (`isAtBoundary`) and stops ticking.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus on either +/− button draws the two-layer halo on the GROUP, not the button: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Informative-Bold` ring (always Informative). Each IconButton's own `:focus-visible` ring is suppressed (`box-shadow: none`).
- The halo selector is `:has(button:focus-visible)` only — focusing the value input to type does not paint it.
- `[data-force-state="focus"]` on the group mirrors the same halo for documentation.

**Keyboard**
- The native input is always mounted (visually hidden until edit). `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` step by `step` (default 1). `Shift+Arrow` uses `largeStep` (`step * shiftMultiplier`, default 10). `Alt+Arrow` uses Base UI's `smallStep`.
- `Home` / `End` jump to `min` / `max` only when those bounds are passed; without them the keys are left to the browser.
- `PageUp` / `PageDown` are not handled.
- Typing digits enters edit mode (`data-editing`): the odometer hides, the input shows its caret, and NumberField commits on `Enter` or blur — not on each keystroke. Arrow-key stepping goes through `setValue`, not a DOM `input` event, so it does not trip edit mode.
- A +/− `pointerdown` sets `steppingRef` so the focus Base UI then moves onto the input (non-touch only) does not swap to edit mode and kill the roll animation.

**Disabled**
- `disabled` adds `.disabled` on the group: `--Disabled-Opacity` and `pointer-events: none`. The ROOT (`:has(.disabled)`) sets `cursor: not-allowed`, so the not-allowed cursor is observable — the opposite of the Button gap, because the cursor lives on the still-hit-testable wrapper.
- `readOnly` is different: the group gets `pointer-events: none` and `cursor: default`, the +/− buttons are `visibility: hidden`, and the input is `readOnly`. It does not dim.
- At min/max only the exhausted IconButton is natively disabled; because that button also has IconButton's `pointer-events: none`, its own `not-allowed` cursor is not observable (the known gap), while the rest of the stepper still works.

**Touch**
- IconButton hover overlays never apply on touch-only devices; the remapped pressed fill plus IconButton's 7% scale-up (clipped by the pill) are the tap response.
- Base UI's stepper-button focus-the-input behaviour is documented as non-touch only, so a finger tap on +/− does not steal focus into the hidden field.

| `attention` | `StepperAttention` | No | - | Attention level controls visual weight. Default: 'medium' |
| `className` | `string` | No | - | Additional class name |

# Switch Machine-Readable Documentation

_Generated from source metadata. Do not edit manually._

## Intent and Purpose

- **Intent**: Immediate binary toggle — state takes effect on change without a submit action.
- **Task contexts**: settings-toggle, feature-flag, live-preference
- **Sentiments**: neutral, positive

## Composition Rules

- **Requires**: label or aria-label
- **Allows**: read-only mode, accent override
- **Forbids**: use in forms requiring explicit submit, replace with Checkbox for non-immediate effects

## Variant Logic

- **default**: use when immediate on/off setting
- **readOnly**: use when display-only permission or system setting

## Relationships and Dependencies

- **Related**: Checkbox, Radio
- **Escalates to**: -
- **Degrades to**: Checkbox
- **Groups with**: -

## Context Signals

- **Density**: compact, default, open
- **Modality**: desktop, mobile
- **Brand**: theme-scope aware, appearance + accent dual-role
- **Mode**: light, dark, surface-context

## Observability Hooks

- **Track**: toggle_on, toggle_off
- **Health**: a11y_violations, adoption_rate

## Interaction Behavior

The track carries the colour and the knob carries the movement, and the two are kept on separate CSS channels so they never fight: the knob's `translateX` lives on the thumb element while its press-scale lives on the thumb's `::before` pseudo-element. Travel distance is derived live in CSS from `trackWidth − knobSize − 2 × padding` rather than being a standalone token, so it stays correct however the switch is themed or ramped. Two things surprise people. First, the unchecked track ignores the `appearance` prop entirely — it follows the nearest `<Surface>`'s role, and Neutral on the bare page or at the palette extremes — while only the checked track follows `appearance`. Second, although the unchecked track rests on the role's `Moderate` step, hovering jumps it to `Subtle-Hover`, because the system has no hover/pressed token for `Moderate`. `readOnly` is a wholly different look from `disabled`: it stays focusable and repaints as a transparent, outlined track with a smaller ink-coloured dot.

**Hover**
- Unchecked, the track fills with `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`; checked, it fills with `--{Role}-Bold-Hover`.
- The unchecked track rests on the role's `Moderate` emphasis but hovers to its `Subtle-Hover` — a different emphasis family. `Moderate` has no hover or pressed token in the system, so the nearest darkened solid surface state is reused.
- The knob is deliberately re-pinned on hover: explicit rules re-assert its fill (`--Surface-Default` unchecked, `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y` checked) so it can never inherit the track's hover tint.
- Every hover rule sits inside `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap leaves no stuck tint behind.
- Every hover rule is also qualified `:not([data-readonly])`, so a read-only switch is completely inert under the pointer.
- Hover changes the fill only — the track never grows, and the knob does not move.

**Press**
- The knob scales UP to `--Switch-thumbPressScale` (1.07 by default). Note the direction: the knob grows, unlike Button which squashes down.
- The scale is applied through the `scale` property on the knob's `::before` layer while `translateX` stays on the knob itself, so the press squash and the slide compose cleanly instead of overwriting one another.
- The track deepens to `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` when unchecked, `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` when checked.
- The track itself never scales — only the knob does.
- Press is not `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so touch gets the same feedback; it IS `:not([data-readonly])`-guarded, so a read-only switch gets none of it.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus draws the standard two-layer halo on the track: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer ring at `calc(--Stroke-XL + --Focus-Outline-Width)`, so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
- The outer ring colour is ALWAYS `--Informative-Bold`, never the appearance role — a `positive` or `negative` switch still focuses informative-blue, per the Figma focus-ring spec.
- `:focus-visible` only; `.switch:focus` merely clears the native outline, so a mouse click paints no ring. A global `[data-force-state="focus"]` ancestor hook forces it on for previews.
- Unlike hover and press, focus is NOT excluded for `readOnly`: the CSS section comment says read-only has "no hover/focus/pressed states", but the halo selector carries no `:not([data-readonly])` and read-only keeps `tabindex="0"` — so a read-only switch does show the focus ring.
- `box-shadow` is in no transition list, so the halo snaps on and off rather than fading.

**Keyboard**
- Base UI renders a `<span role="switch">`, not a native `<button>`, and synthesises activation through its button helper: `Enter` activates on keydown and `Space` on keyup, matching native button convention.
- Form submission is carried by a hidden `<input type="checkbox">` rendered alongside the span, so `name` still round-trips through a form.
- `disabled` sets `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"` — removed from the tab order but still announced. It does NOT use a native `disabled` attribute.
- `readOnly` sets `aria-readonly="true"`, does not set `aria-disabled`, and keeps `tabindex="0"` — so it stays reachable by `Tab`, unlike disabled.
- The control is wrapped in a `<label>`, so clicking the label text toggles the switch too.
- Switch adds no keyboard shortcuts of its own beyond the primitive's activation keys.

**Selected / checked**
- Checked fills the track with `--{Role}-Bold` and paints the knob `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y`; unchecked fills the track with the surface-resolved `Moderate` and pins the knob to `--Surface-Default` (white).
- Which role fills the CHECKED track comes from `appearance` (`auto` or unset resolves to `secondary`). The UNCHECKED track deliberately ignores `appearance` and uses the nearest `<Surface>`'s role, falling back to Neutral on the bare page and at the palette extremes (surface steps 2500 and 100).
- The knob's travel is computed in CSS from the live geometry — `trackWidth − knobSize − 2 × padding` — never from a separate `travel` token, so the knob keeps landing exactly at the far padding edge under any theme or size ramp.
- Under `[dir="rtl"]` the travel sign flips via `--_sw-inline-sign: -1`, so the knob slides right-to-left.
- `accent` (primary / secondary / sparkle) overrides ONLY the checked fill and leaves the appearance role's context colours alone — `appearance="neutral" accent="sparkle"` gives a grey context with a purple fill. `readOnly` drops any accent.
- The Figma matrix chrome sometimes labels the boolean `selected`; there is no `selected` prop in React — use `checked` / `defaultChecked`.

**Disabled**
- `disabled` dims the whole `<label>` row to `--Disabled-Opacity`, sets `cursor: not-allowed` on that wrapper, and puts `pointer-events: none` on the track.
- Here the `not-allowed` cursor IS observable: the track is `pointer-events: none`, so the pointer falls through to the `<label>` wrapper, which declares `not-allowed` and keeps its pointer events. This is unlike a natively `disabled` control (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
- `readOnly` is a different look, not a dim. The wrapper gets `data-readonly` and is explicitly excluded from the opacity rule, the cursor stays `default`, and the track repaints as transparent with a `--Stroke-M` outline in `--Text-High`, padding bumped from `--Spacing-0-5` to `--Spacing-1`, and a knob two f-steps smaller filled with the role's `Bold` ink.
- The read-only knob is painted through the thumb's `::before` fill channel, not `background-color` on the thumb — setting the latter is hidden behind the opaque pseudo-element, which is why the dot used to always render white.
- `readOnly` also forces both the checked and unchecked state roles to `neutral`.
- Figma's API table has a row labelled `loading` that actually describes disabled behaviour; the component set has no loading variant and React exposes no `loading` prop — use `disabled`.

**Touch**
- Hover tints never apply on touch-only devices; the pressed track tint plus the knob's +7% growth are the entire tap response.
- The track is only `--Spacing-7` / `--Spacing-9` / `--Spacing-10` wide (28 / 36 / 40px) at sizes S / M / L, and its height is just knob + 2 × padding — well under the 44px mobile minimum.
- The `<label>` wrapper extends the hit area across the label text, but nothing pads the row to 44px; add your own spacing when you need the mobile touch-target minimum.

| `appearance` | `SwitchAppearance` | No | - | Multi-accent appearance role. Interactive checked: explicit role wins; 'auto'/unset resolves to secondary. Interactive unchecked: ignores this prop and uses nearest Surface appearance, then neutral. ReadOnly: neutral in both visual states. | `aria-labelledby` | `string` | No | - | ID of an element that labels the switch. |
| `checked` | `boolean` | No | - | Whether the switch is on (controlled). Figma component property: `checked` (matrix chrome may say `selected`). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | No | - | Label text |
| `className` | `string` | No | - | Additional class name |
| `data-testid` | `string` | No | - | Stable anchor for QA / e2e — forwarded to the root switch control only (not the label wrapper). |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | No | - | Default state (uncontrolled) |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | No | - | Whether the switch is disabled (non-interactive, dimmed). Figma API table mislabels this row as `loading` with a disabled description — the component set has no loading variant; use `disabled`. |
| `id` | `string` | No | - | HTML id attribute |
| `name` | `string` | No | - | Field name for form submission |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | No | - | Change handler — fires with the next checked value |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | No | - | Whether the switch is read-only (visually distinct from disabled; remains focusable) |
| `size` | `SwitchSize` | No | - | Size preset. Default: 'm' |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | No | - | Inline styles |

## Intent and Purpose

- **Intent**: Accessible tabbed navigation on Base UI Tabs. Figma node 1:55592: inactive labels use content/low (`--Text-Low`), selected labels use content/high (`--Text-High`), accent is the indicator bar only (`--Primary-Tinted` / colour/content/tinted). Not TintedA11y on labels.
- **Task contexts**: -
- **Sentiments**: neutral

## Composition Rules

- **Requires**: -
- **Allows**: start, end
- **Forbids**: -

## Variant Logic

- **horizontal**: use when Horizontal
- **vertical**: use when Vertical

## Relationships and Dependencies

- **Related**: -
- **Escalates to**: -
- **Degrades to**: -
- **Groups with**: -

## Context Signals

- **Density**: compact, default, open
- **Modality**: desktop, mobile
- **Brand**: theme-scope aware, recipe-driven
- **Mode**: light, dark, surface-context

## Observability Hooks

- **Track**: -
- **Health**: a11y_violations

## Interaction Behavior

Tabs are Base UI tabs with OneUI chrome on top: hover and press recolour the label and slots only — the state-layer stay transparent in every state, and the selected bar is a single list-level indicator that slides between tabs rather than a per-tab underline. Default activation is manual: arrow keys move focus without changing the selected tab; `Enter` / `Space` commit. Pass `activateOnFocus` to make arrows select immediately.

**Hover**
- Only an unselected tab changes on hover: the label steps to `--Neutral-High` (overridable via `--Tabs-colorHover`) and the start / end slots step to `--Neutral-Tinted`.
- The padded state-layer stays `transparent` — there is no hover fill and the selected indicator does not appear under an unselected tab.
- Wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck hover colour behind.
- Selected tabs (`[data-active]`) and disabled tabs are excluded from every hover rule, so the selected label already at `--Neutral-High` does not flicker.

**Press**
- An unselected press drops the label and both slots to `--Neutral-Low` (overridable via `--Tabs-colorPressed` / `--Tabs-iconColorPressed`).
- Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a touch tap gets the same colour drop a mouse press does.
- The start-slot icon scales UP to `1.14` while the tab is held — the label and end slot do not move. This selector does not exclude `[data-active]`, so a selected tab with a start icon still grows on press. This is opposite to Button, which scales the whole control DOWN.
- Selected tabs are excluded from press colour (`:not([data-active])`), so the already-active label does not drop to `--Neutral-Low`.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo on the inner state-layer, not the tab button: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring, so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
- `:focus` on the tab only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click does not paint it.
- The panel uses a simpler `outline` in `--Focus-Outline` at `--Focus-Outline-Width` when it is itself `:focus-visible` — it does not use the two-layer halo.

**Keyboard**
- Default `activateOnFocus={false}`: `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` (horizontal) or `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` (vertical) move focus only — the previously selected tab stays selected until `Enter` or `Space`.
- `activateOnFocus` flips that: the same arrows both move focus and select immediately (Base UI automatic activation).
- `Home` / `End` jump focus to the first / last tab. `loopFocus` defaults to `true`, so arrows wrap at the ends.
- Disabled tabs stay in the arrow path: Base UI Tabs marks them `aria-disabled` with `focusableWhenDisabled`, and the list passes an empty `disabledIndices` array, so arrows land on them. They still refuse `Enter` / `Space` / click.
- A value change also smooth-scrolls the selected tab into the overflowing list viewport, without using `scrollIntoView` (that would scroll ancestor pages).

**Selected / checked**
- The selected tab's label is `--Neutral-High` and its start / end slots switch to `--{Role}-Tinted` — label stays Neutral; only the icon takes the appearance role.
- Font weight stays `--Label-FontWeight-Medium` when selected, so the row does not shift as tabs activate.
- The selected bar is a list-level indicator in `--{Role}-Tinted` (overridable via `--Tabs-indicatorColor`). It tracks Base UI's `--active-tab-*` vars and is inset by the state-layer padding so it underlines the content, not the padded tab.
- Horizontal: a bottom bar of `--Stroke-XL` thickness. Vertical: a left bar whose height is centred in the active tab.
- Selected is exposed as `aria-selected` and `[data-active]` by Base UI.

**Disabled**
- A disabled tab dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and recolours the label to `--Primary-Low`.
- Base UI keeps it `aria-disabled` rather than natively `disabled`, so it remains focusable and `cursor: not-allowed` on the tab is actually observable — unlike Button, there is no `pointer-events: none`.
- Hover and press colour, and the start-slot press scale, are all suppressed via `:not([data-disabled])`.
- Click, `Enter`, and `Space` do not activate it; tests confirm `aria-selected` stays `false`.

**Touch**
- On touch-only devices the hover colour never applies; the pressed `--Neutral-Low` label plus the start-slot scale-up are the entire tap response.
- Pointer-move hover tracking is not used — unlike SegmentedControl, Tabs has no sliding hover pill.

_Generated from source metadata. Do not edit manually._

## Intent and Purpose

- **Intent**: Floating label that attaches to a trigger element. The canonical API follows Figma: position, tip, disable, delay, hideDelay, offset, and portal; deprecated Base UI-style aliases remain compatible.
- **Task contexts**: tooltip, hint, popup, hover, overlay
- **Sentiments**: neutral

## Composition Rules

- **Requires**: children, content
- **Allows**: -
- **Forbids**: -

## Variant Logic

- **default**: use when Default

## Relationships and Dependencies

- **Related**: -
- **Escalates to**: -
- **Degrades to**: -
- **Groups with**: -

## Context Signals

- **Density**: compact, default, open
- **Modality**: desktop, mobile
- **Brand**: theme-scope aware, recipe-driven
- **Mode**: light, dark, surface-context

## Observability Hooks

- **Track**: -
- **Health**: a11y_violations

## Interaction Behavior

A non-modal floating label. Default `trigger="hover"` waits 200ms before opening (a pass-through under 200ms never shows it) and, with `hoverable` default true, stays open if the pointer moves onto the bubble. `trigger="click"` and `trigger="focus"` open with zero delay. Not focus-trapped, no scroll lock, no inert page. `disable` / `disabled` prevent every trigger mode from opening. Children are wrapped in a `<span>` so Base UI events still attach when the child (for example Button) does not spread DOM props. On open the popup fades and slides in from a 5px per-side offset (top eases from `translateY(5px)`, bottom from `-5px`, left/right the equivalent on X) while the arrow translates from its retracted `--tip-translate` to `0 0` in sync — open runs `--Motion-Duration-M` / `--Motion-Easing-Entrance-Moderate`, close swaps the timing to `--Motion-Easing-Exit-Moderate`. Subtle/reduced-motion (and `data-instant` inside a provider delay group) collapse this to an opacity-only fade with the transform and arrow held at 0.

**Hover**
- Default `trigger="hover"`: the tooltip opens after `delay` (200ms, overriding Base UI's 600ms). A cursor that leaves before that elapses never opens it.
- `hideDelay` (alias `closeDelay`) delays hide on unhover; when omitted, hide timing is Base UI's default.
- `hoverable` default true (`disableHoverablePopup={!hoverable}`) lets the pointer travel onto the popup without closing. Set `hoverable={false}` to close as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger.
- The trigger wrapper is visually inert (`cursor: inherit`, no fill). Hover feedback lives on the child, not the tooltip.
- Inside a `TooltipProvider` delay group, sliding the pointer from one trigger to an adjacent one opens the next tooltip with no delay and no entrance transition: Base UI sets `data-instant` on the popup (when it opens during the group's instant phase, or closes because a sibling opened) and OneUI answers with `transition: none`. A standalone tooltip with no provider never receives `data-instant`, so it always plays its normal transition.

**Press**
- `trigger="click"` toggles on the trigger press, with `delay={0}` / `closeDelay={0}` so it does not wait for the hover timer.
- A pointer-down outside the trigger or portalled popup closes click and focus tooltips. `trigger="manual"` does not add that outside-press listener.
- Hover-mode outside-press is left to Base UI (unhover / dismiss), not the extra document listener.

**Focus**
- `trigger="focus"` opens on focus and closes on blur. OneUI calls `preventBaseUIHandler` so Base UI's internal focus open never runs — OneUI's own focus/blur handlers own the state.
- Hover mode still opens from keyboard focus via Base UI's native tooltip focus behaviour — OneUI does not add a second listener there.
- The tooltip is not a focus trap. Focus stays on the trigger; the popup is `role="tooltip"` while open.
- While closed but `keepMounted`, the retained node is `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden`, so it is not announced.

**Keyboard**
- `Escape` closes click, focus, and manual tooltips via a document `keydown` listener (WCAG dismiss-on-request). Hover mode uses Base UI `useDismiss` instead of that extra listener.
- There is no Tab trap. `Tab` from a `trigger="focus"` tooltip blurs the trigger and closes it.
- Click/focus/manual cancel Base UI `trigger-hover` / `trigger-focus` / `trigger-press` open events so those reasons cannot open the tooltip behind the OneUI handlers. `escape-key` and `outside-press` are allowed through.

**Disabled**
- `disable` (canonical) or deprecated `disabled` is passed to Base UI as `disabled`. Hover, click, and focus all refuse to open.
- When both aliases are passed with different values, `disable` wins.

**Touch**
- Hover-open is mouse-only (`mouseOnly` on Base UI's hover interaction). A finger tap does not start the 200ms hover timer.
- A tap that focuses the trigger can still open the default tooltip through Base UI's focus path. Use `trigger="click"` when the open affordance must be an explicit tap/toggle.

## Observability Hooks

## Interaction Behavior

TouchSlider is a chunky single-thumb fill control: there is no visible knob. The whole 32px pill is the hit target (with a 44px slop via a pseudo-element), a tap anywhere on the track moves the fill to that point — the value jumps but the fill eases across via a real `width`/`height` transition rather than snapping — and a drag captures the pointer on the Control. The thumb is a zero-size, `pointer-events: none` host for the hidden range input. Keyboard uses the same macOS-style accelerator as Slider.

**Press**
- Pointer-down anywhere on the Control — including the hit-slop `::before` that extends the 32px pill to 44px — is a track press: Base UI jumps the (invisible) thumb to that point and then `setPointerCapture`s for the drag.
- There is no separate thumb to grab; `pointer-events: none` on `.thumb` makes every press hit the track.
- The start-slot icon is `inert` and `pointer-events: none`, so a tap on the leading cap still drags the fill rather than activating the icon.
- `onValueCommitted` fires on release, matching Slider.

**Focus**
- Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo on the CONTROL (the pill), not on a knob: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Informative-Bold` ring (always Informative, regardless of appearance).
- The selector is `:has(:focus-visible)`, not `:focus-within`, so a mouse click that focuses the hidden input does not paint the halo.
- There is no value tooltip.

**Keyboard**
- The same capture-phase accelerator as Slider intercepts `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (horizontal) or `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (vertical), `PageUp` / `PageDown`, and `Shift+Arrow`. Repeats accelerate (×2 / ×5 / `largeStep`); `Shift` and page keys always use `largeStep`.
- `Home` / `End` fall through to Base UI and jump to `min` / `max`.
- On a horizontal TouchSlider, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` are not accelerated; they fall through and Base UI steps them by Root's `step` (TouchSlider always passes the public `step`, unlike Slider's `dragStep`). Same for `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` when vertical.
- `readOnly` sets `aria-readonly`, keeps the input focusable (not natively disabled), and both cancels Base UI changes and skips the accelerator. `disabled` natively disables the input.

**Disabled**
- `disabled` dims the root to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed`. The Control, its hit-slop `::before`, the thumb, and the input all get `pointer-events: none`.
- The not-allowed cursor is on the root, so it is observable — this is not the Button-style cursor gap.
- `readOnly` is stricter than Slider's: the whole root gets `pointer-events: none` (cursor `default` on the Control), so pointer dragging is blocked, while the input stays focusable for AT. It does not dim.

**Touch**
- The visual pill is `--Spacing-8` (32px) thick; `.control::before` extends the hit area by `--TouchSlider-hitSlop` (`--Spacing-Negative-1-5`) so the target is 44px without changing layout. Because the slop belongs to Base UI's Control, presses in that extra band still jump-and-drag.
- Root and Control set `touch-action: none` so a drag does not scroll the page.
- There is no hover fill or knob growth — a tap's only visual is the fill easing into place: `.indicator` transitions its `width` / `height` over `--Motion-Duration-M` with `--Motion-Easing-Entrance-Moderate`, so it glides to the new point rather than snapping there. `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps only the colour fade and drops the size animation.
